quotes.text: The built-in Copilot features help you move through tasks faster. They give you information, they fill in fields, they suggest text, but you're still the one doing the work. Agents are different because they can act on your behalf.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws the core line between assistive Copilot features and agents that act.

quotes.text: They use something called co-pilot credits, which is basically a usage-based currency for AI actions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the billing model of Business Central agents in one sentence.

quotes.text: Agents inherit the exact same permission model as human users. They can only see data you've authorized. If a user can't access a certain customer record, the agent can't either.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the security principle that agents are bound by existing permissions.

quotes.text: It's not about replacing people. It's about removing the repetitive error-prone parts so you can focus on what actually needs human judgment, negotiating pricing, handling exceptions, or building relationships with customers.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames agents as removing repetitive work rather than replacing people.

quotes.text: The rule here is simple. Grant the minimum permissions just like you would for a new hire.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a memorable, actionable governance rule for agent permissions.

chapters.title: What Copilot in Business Central is
From email to order: a scenario

takeaways: Built-in Copilot features in Business Central such as analysis assist, autofill and bank reconciliation are included in the license at no extra cost.
Microsoft-built agents like the Sales Order Agent and Payables Agent act in the background but consume Copilot credits and require human approval for critical actions.
Custom agents can be created with the Agent Designer from plain-English instructions, and they inherit the same permission model and billing as Microsoft's agents.
hook: Business Central users keep hearing about Copilot and agents but rarely know what is free, what costs money and what actually does work for them. This episode walks finance and operations teams through the three layers: built-in features, Microsoft-built agents and custom agents, including Copilot credit costs and security controls.
